title: Deploy backs up before it migrates, and migrate_down can undo it
description:
SPIDR child 3 of task-8f86e10504c74e248ccfa6f427b41a15 (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). dependsOn child 1 (task-463f195efd2f4fd2886790029a474194, the tool) and child 2 (task-ff41c5c9efa34494b7b91e6f0ddcb7c2, the disposable-database lifecycle this reuses). PROOF ROW: it owns the UI, the live drive and the docs (global rail 21).

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: applying pending migrations on deploy AFTER a `pg_dump` backup; the `moe-migration-receipt/1` record; the human-only `deployment.migrate_down`; the Deployments and node cards; and the live drive.

BACKUP BEFORE MIGRATE IS THE ORDER, and it is the only thing standing between a bad migration and lost production data. The backup goes to `<project>/.moe-next/backups/<env>/<ts>.sql` with its sha256 in the receipt - note `.moe-next/backups` is an EXISTING convention (apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/activation-receipts-measure.ts:32-33 already defines BACKUP_DIRECTORY '.moe-next' and BACKUP_LEAF 'backups'), so reuse it rather than inventing a second location. MIGRATION_BACKUP_FAILED means NOTHING IS APPLIED - a migration that ran after a failed backup is the exact scenario this receipt exists to make impossible.

CROSS-ROW COORDINATION, NOT A DEPENDENCY: 'applies on deploy' needs the deploy path, which belongs to task-5d30948435524c6fa2789e1c033aafe7 (containerized deployment) - a SIBLING feature row, and the parent rail forbids depending on one. Build the migration-on-deploy step so it composes with that row's deploy rather than duplicating it, and if the deploy path does not exist yet, land the migrate/backup/receipt machinery with its own entry point and say so in the record. Also: the environment's DATABASE_URL comes from the environments model (task-9ae492b373fa4e7aa6b1e91585f6e612's children) - same coordination, same rule.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04): no deploy path, no migration receipt, no backup-before-migrate anywhere.
definitionOfDone: BACKUP-BEFORE-MIGRATE ORDERING is asserted through injectable docker/pg ports in an offline test: the `pg_dump` completes before the first migration runs, and MIGRATION_BACKUP_FAILED means ZERO migrations were applied - assert the schema is untouched on that path, not merely that a refusal was returned. This is the row's central safety property.

`moe-migration-receipt/1` records {environment, sha, applied[], backupRef, APPLIED|REFUSED(code)|REVERTED} and is read back from a real store with every member asserted. backupRef is NULLABLE: a failed dump yields backupRef:null with REFUSED(MIGRATION_BACKUP_FAILED). When present it carries the backup's sha256 and the file exists at `<project>/.moe-next/backups/pre-migration/<env>/<ts>.sql` - the EXISTING pre-migration convention (task-0a56ecee), not a second location.

`deployment.migrate_down` published HUMAN-ONLY and MCP-EXCLUDED with the full roster backfill and a bidirectional set-equality roster test; it reverts the last batch and its receipt records the revert. Assert the schema actually changed back, not merely that the command returned.

THE RESTORE PATH: when a down-migration cannot revert, restoring the recorded backup is possible and its receipt says so. Assert a restore round trip against a real disposable PostgreSQL - a backup nobody has ever restored is a file, not a safety net.
MIGRATION_BACKUP_FAILED and MIGRATION_FAILED (with the failing file) assert code + layer; MIGRATION_FAILED on deploy leaves the receipt REFUSED with the failing migration named.

The Deployments card shows migration state per environment (pending/applied, last backup), a node card shows 'adds migration NNNN', and Runs shows migration receipts - three surfaces, all CONSUMING producer rows: declared identifiers come ONLY through task-122b55fd's authority + `/runs/read` path; project/environment receipt observations come ONLY through task-8f1f15bc's bounded reads. 'Pending' requires an actual admitted environment/workspace/DB observation from those reads - never declaration-minus-receipt-history, never missing-evidence => none (missing is UNKNOWN). The environment column's UI source is board-lanes, not goal-nodes. This parent stays proof/presentation-only: no daemon or contract edits. Playwright against a REAL daemon; `pnpm test:e2e:browser` count line quoted.

LIVE DRIVE: a real migration verified on a disposable PostgreSQL and applied to the PREVIEW environment - the receipt and the `\dt` listing in a row comment under ~4500 chars. If no preview environment exists yet (the deployment row is a sibling and may not have landed), record that plainly and drive the verified half only. Runbook + README updated; gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`.
taskRails: BACKUP BEFORE MIGRATE, ALWAYS. A failed backup means nothing is applied. This is the row's reason for existing and the one property whose failure loses data that cannot be recovered.
RESTORE MUST BE PROVEN, not assumed. A backup that has never been restored in a test is a file, not a safety net.
REUSE `.moe-next/backups` (activation-receipts-measure.ts:32-33). A second backup location is a second place to look during an incident.

COMPOSE WITH THE DEPLOY ROW, do not duplicate it: task-5d30948435524c6fa2789e1c033aafe7 owns the deploy path and is a SIBLING feature row (no dependsOn allowed). If it has not landed, ship this row's machinery behind its own entry point and say so.
`deployment.migrate_down` IS HUMAN-ONLY. Reverting a production schema is never an agent's decision.
